mail.pick: Pick a message to read it
mail.remoteImages: Pictures from other sites are not loaded, so the sender cannot tell when you read this.

compose.title: New message
compose.subject: Subject
compose.noRecipient: Add at least one address to send to.
compose.noFolders: Your mailbox has no Drafts or Sent folder yet; try again in a minute.
compose.noIdentity: Your mailbox has no sender address yet; ask an admin.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Passwords for mail apps such as Outlook, Thunderbird or your phone's Mail. Each app gets its own, so you can remove one without changing the others.
devices.addDetail: Name the app or device, so you know which password to remove later.
devices.name: Name
devices.nameHint: Such as iPhone or Work laptop
devices.madeDetail: Enter these in the app now. The password is not shown again.
devices.none: No devices yet. The webmail needs none.
devices.settingsDetail: Use these with a device password; your sign-in password does not work in apps.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: The domains and mailboxes in the domains file. They are changed there, and the mail server follows within a minute.
domains.noneDetail: Add your first domain and mailboxes to the domains file:
domains.serverDetail: Other mail servers reach this one at this name; each domain's MX record points to it.

domain.description: Its mailboxes, and the DNS records its mail needs.

dns.title: DNS records
dns.description: Whether mail for this domain arrives here and is trusted when it is sent.
dns.name: Where
dns.noSelectorDetail: Set dkimSelector for this domain in the domains file to the selector the mail server signs with, and its record is checked too.

sync.title: Mail server
sync.description: Mail keeps the server in step with the file after each change and every five minutes.
sync.changed: {{created}} created, {{updated}} updated, {{disabled}} disabled the last time.

file.error: The domains file has a mistake; the last good version is still in use

settings.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of Mail for access.
settings.accountDetail: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.
settings.membersDetail: Who can sign in to Mail, and with which role. Users read their own mail; viewers also see the domains and mailboxes; admins also sync the server and manage members and tokens.
settings.signinDetail: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.
settings.tokensDetail: For scripts. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once. Tokens cannot read anyone's mail.
